questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language, culture and art, the academic environment and research

questions.answer: Relatively easy, the host university was quite helpful in providing information and answering my questions

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through contacts and network

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's highly recommended. I have tried university housing before and it was not very nice, but of course housing off campus can be difficult to find.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very chaotic process

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I foudn courses online and then had to email all the professors to find out how many ECTS-credits the courses gave, and in some instances they didn't know. Then I attended a bunch of courses in the first week to find out what I liked, which was nice, and then registered the courses in 'Campus Management', an online system that does not work very well. For some of the courses I could not register and just contacted the professors.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could ask my Erasmus coordinator or the Erasmus Incoming-team.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to relax and trust that it will all work out, but it takes a long time. And show up for the classes you want to attend, even if you cannot register - talk to the professors, they are often very nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was confused about the level in some courses, since I only took MA classes but there were still BA students attending. Some of the courses had a quite high level, where some felt a bit more like BA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite different and generally more involving, which I found nice. But there was also less evaluation and student influence on the way the classes were taught than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Rituality and Theatre
- Energy Flows
- Music and Dream: Dreams in Music Theatre
- On the way to a new opera
- Choreographic Interventions
- Utopia, Hope and Negativity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The course 'Unterwegs zu einer neuen Oper' was particularly interesting because it was a cooperation between the university, the art school and the opera house. Such courses don't exist at UCPH (in my field at least) so that was exiting. The lecture series 'Energy Flows' was also very interesting, and good for exchange students who need classes in English.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had very few unexpected costs. The main one was the apartment I rented was not as well equipped as I expected, so I had to buy a few household items.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Art and culture had a big post in my budget, but thanks to the student discounts I spend much less than expected though going to the theatre/museum/opera/etc. at least once a week. Food, drink, household etc. was more expensive than I expected. The prises in Berlin have risen since I was there last.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different stuff - almost any athletic or cultural activity you can think of. I joined a choir and a dance class, at it was wonderful.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choir is a great place to meet people and get local friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the theatre, there's so much great stuff. And if the wheather is nice, go to Tempelhofer Feld.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I've lived there before.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Follow your interests - take classes in dance/sport/music/ceramics/yoga/politics/whatever your interests are. And if people from the uni-courses seem nice, ask to go 'Mensen' together

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: When to say 'Sie' and when to say 'Du'

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation for art and culture + the political directness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Challenge yourself in terms of language - I think it's often easier to get help etc. if you at least try to ask in German, and some of the most interesting courses are in German. You can learn it!
2. Sign up for a unisport-course or something
3. If you can, prioritize to live in the city over living near the university. You will travel far everyday no matter what.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's okay not to attend every Erasmus-activity.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Strengthening my language skills, deepening my relationship with the city and people in it, exploring a ton of art and culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus bureaucracy

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
